name: Active extension probe (AED)
plain: Fetches a hidden file from each of thousands of known extension IDs to learn which ones are installed.
meaning: Reveals installed add-ons, which can imply job search, sales role, religion, health or politics, and a stable identifier for the browser profile. LinkedIn calls it abuse prevention; critics call it covert profiling.

web.api: fetch('chrome-extension://<id>/<file>') per list entry, Promise.allSettled; fulfilled = installed

access.persistence: Runs on page load for every visit; result is sent once per run if any ID is found
steps: Script checks navigator.userAgent contains 'Chrome' and that it is not server side
For each hardcoded {id, file} pair, fetch chrome-extension://id/file
A fulfilled fetch means the extension is installed and exposes that file in web_accessible_resources
Collected IDs are sent as AedEvent.browserExtensionIds through the tracking payload, only if the list is non-empty
Later versions add staggered scanning, requestIdleCallback and a 2000 ms timeout (per BrowserGate)

edge.note: Chromium Edge: UA contains Chrome, extension IDs from the Chrome Web Store work if installed there

firefox.note: moz-extension URLs use per-install random UUIDs, so IDs cannot be guessed

safari.note: Safari extension URLs are per-install random

chrome_android.note: Chrome for Android has no extension support

data.metric: Set of installed extension IDs out of the probe list
data.update: every page load or session start

fields.name: browserExtensionIds
fields.range: 0 to list size (2,953 in the public snapshot, 6,236 claimed Apr 2026)

limits.headline: Can check which of thousands of known browser extensions you have installed
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when you open the site in Chrome or Edge.
can: Test a long list of known extension IDs, one by one
Tell which of those extensions are installed
Use the result as a stable fingerprint of your browser profile
Send the list of detected extensions to its servers
cannot: See extensions that are not on its list
See what an extension does or the data inside it
Work in Firefox, Safari or most phone browsers
Find extensions that keep their files hidden from web pages
limits.differs: Works in Chrome and Edge only. Firefox, Safari and phone browsers block it.

story.what_it_is: A site quietly tests thousands of known browser add-on addresses to learn which add-ons you have installed.
story.for_you: You see nothing at all. While the page loads, it tries thousands of hidden add-on addresses in the background. The answer is a list of which add-ons your browser has.
story.for_makers: The site says this catches scraping and automation tools that break its rules. Critics say the same list can hint at your job, beliefs or health, and acts as a steady ID for your browser.

use_cases.example: A professional network checks for known scraper add-ons when a profile gets viewed hundreds of times in a minute, then limits the account.
A sneaker or concert ticket site looks for auto-buyer add-ons before a big drop and sends those visitors to extra checks.
A browser game with real prizes looks for auto-clicker or cheat add-ons before a ranked match starts.
An ad network adds the add-on list to its other clues so it can tell a returning browser from a new one.
A fraud team compares add-on lists across thousands of new accounts and finds a cluster of fake profiles that all share the same odd set.
A sales software maker spots a rival's sales add-on in a visitor's browser, which critics call competitor snooping.
A platform could guess that someone is job hunting from a resume or job alert add-on, which privacy groups warn about.

technical_bounds: Only Chromium browsers with chrome-extension:// URLs
Only finds extensions that list a file in web_accessible_resources
Manifest V3 use_dynamic_url randomizes the URL so those extensions cannot be probed
Cannot read extension data, only presence

legit_uses: Detect scraper and automation extensions that abuse the site
abuse: Profiling users by installed extensions (religion, health, job hunting, rivals' tools)

linkedin.how: Core of BrowserGate. LinkedIn script loops a hardcoded extension ID list (2,953 IDs in the public mdp snapshot, 6,236 claimed Apr 2026) and fetches each chrome-extension:// resource. Verified in the snapshot; LinkedIn says it is for abuse prevention.
